title: Baker's poor rhythm versus Bobrovsky's intonation
summary: Baker plays off time and is hard to work with; Bobrovsky, whom Duerr worked with for ten years, plays everything right on the beat.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Well I worked at Brenham's Four once with this Baker guy, and Baker, he plays a lot of violin but he trues you sometimes, you know. Well he's playing ad lib stuff, you know. He plays off time. He plays off time. I know I work with him too. You work with him? Well then you know what I'm talking about. He has no fearful rhythm. I work with him at Lothar too. You know you can play ad lib but still you can play in rhythm, you know what I mean? But he plays-
He can't play in rhythm once he starts trying to live.
Oh he can't, he's hard to work with. I'm one of the few guys that I put up with a lot of stuff working with. But I like to play and it was the only thing I know.
Yeah I worked with him too there at Lothars for a while. You did?
Guitar? It was piano and guitar. We'd sit down and play for a while and then we'd walk around and pick up the guitar.
But he's hard to work with I tell you. No sense of meter at all.
No. He plays a lot of tunes that you never know.

But he's got a lot of technique though. Yeah. And he knows a lot of tunes and he knows different Greek tunes and stuff and Hungarian stuff. A lot of times he tries to get me to learn the Hungarian stuff but he's faking them himself. He's not playing them right I know. You know what I mean? He's trying to tell me, he always plays like an exercise. It sounds Hungarian style, you know what I mean? But it's not maybe the authentic thing. You know what I mean? No, no. Now when he plays two guitars, I play with Bobrovsky and Bobrovsky plays it right. He plays at the symphony. I mean I worked at Arnold's for about ten years with Bobrovsky on the violin and Gaspar on the card and Bobrovsky plays just another thing on the ground but when he plays a note it sounds like a million dollars because he's got intonation so fine and he plays real good. But he played like two guitars and charters, he'd play them right. When I try to play with this fella, I can't do it with him. He fouls me off. I mean I have to try to foul him but I mean he'd get you all fouled up.
Yeah, that's the way it is. A lot of people like that.

Even a Viennese thing, they try to play, play some of the Viennese waltzes. He plays and he gets all off mute and stuff. I play him with Bobrovsky, he's playing him everything is right, you know, right on the beat.
They got a little group playing there at the German restaurant at Karls. At Karls? Yeah, I was there one night at the Accordion and violin.
